title: CO.LAB Selects Four Startups for Inaugural CO.LAB Q Commercialization Studio in Chattanooga - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Chattanooga accelerator CO.LAB launched CO.LAB Q, a 12-month quantum commercialization studio whose first cohort (RidgeQuantum, Superquantum, esoteriq, Kottackal Business Solutions) will pilot QKD, compilation, data-encoding and sensing products against regional infrastructure, backed by EPB, Quantinuum, Quantum Machines, Classiq and ORNL.

insights.claim: CO.LAB Q's inaugural cohort, starting November 2026 for 12 months, comprises RidgeQuantum, Superquantum, esoteriq and Kottackal Business Solutions.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: An early-stage deal-flow list for quantum application startups in the US Southeast.
insights.locator: Chattanooga startup accelerator The Company Lab

insights.claim: RidgeQuantum is commercializing ORNL-licensed continuous-variable QKD hardware built on standard telecom components and validating it over EPB fiber for critical infrastructure security.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: National-lab IP licensing to startups is a channel for QKD commercialization on existing telecom gear.

insights.claim: esoteriq is building Rune to estimate the cost and feasibility of encoding classical datasets onto physical QPUs using representative customer workloads.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Data-loading overhead is a recognized bottleneck; tools quantifying it may help buyers avoid poor-fit quantum projects.

insights.claim: Superquantum benchmarks logical resource estimation, optimization and execution tooling across hardware platforms, while Kottackal integrates quantum electromagnetic sensors, secure networking and data fusion for asset-monitoring pilots with energy and battery operators.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Cohort leans toward infrastructure and tooling plays rather than hardware.

insights.claim: Founding partners include EPB, Quantinuum, Davidson Technologies, UTC, Middle Tennessee Electric, Quantum Machines and Classiq, with research collaboration from Oak Ridge National Laboratory.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Utility-led regional quantum ecosystems are attracting major vendors as partners.
insights.locator: Supported by founding partners including EPB

insights.claim: The program leverages EPB Quantum Center's on-premises IonQ Forte Enterprise trapped-ion system and a municipal quantum communications network.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A municipal utility owning quantum hardware and networks is an unusual demand-side model.

insights.claim: The studio is designed to bridge the gap between technical proof-of-concept and enterprise deployment, with readiness assessments and periodic advisory-board reviews against commercial milestones.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Implies the main bottleneck for quantum startups is commercialization, not technology.
insights.quote: designed to bridge the gap between technical proof-of-concept and enterprise deployment
insights.locator: Chattanooga startup accelerator The Company Lab
